note: How the Core's physiology maps to the Pulse Physiology Engine (Kitware, Apache-2.0) for the parity experiment and the adapter (p1-pulse-physiology-s02 and s03). Pulse is run server-side or offline by tools/pulse/pulse_bridge.py; its outputs are recorded as traces (content/physio/pulse_traces) and the Core replays a trace through PulseTraceEngine, so a session stays deterministic. Nothing here changes LitePhysio, which stays the default engine.
pulse_build: Kitware Pulse, branch stable, built on Windows with MinGW-w64 GCC 16 (see tools/pulse/README.md)

outputs.note: Pulse's default vitals carry the skin temperature; the Core's Temp is a core-temperature reading, so only the direction of a change is compared

unmapped.EFF-ANAPHYLAXIS: the Pulse Python patient actions contain no anaphylaxis; LitePhysio keeps it
unmapped.PAT-NORMAL: a pattern with no targets: nothing to map
unmapped.PAT-SEPSIS: Pulse's sepsis is a patient condition that needs a 90-second stabilisation of a patient file and its authors mark the model incomplete; not used
unmapped.PAT-DEHYDRATION: Pulse offers a dehydration condition only through stabilisation of a patient file; the haemorrhage scenario covers volume loss
unmapped.PAT-INFECTION: no infection model in the actions used
unmapped.PAT-AF: an arrhythmia action exists but sets a rhythm, not the Core's pattern of rate and pressure
unmapped.EFF-ANALGESIA: a morphine bolus would change several things at once; the Core's analgesia lowers a pain score that Pulse does not carry
unmapped.EFF-ANTIEMETIC: nausea is not a Pulse variable
unmapped.EFF-ANTIBIOTIC: no physiological effect in either engine
unmapped.EFF-POTASSIUM-LOWER: no physiological effect in the Core model
unmapped.EFF-GLUCOSE-RISE: glucose is a Core variable with no Pulse output used here
unmapped.variables: pain, nausea, sedation, glucose and volume_deficit are Core-only variables; Pulse supplies HR, SBP, DBP, RR, SpO2 and a temperature
